**D.** Common-law arson requires malice, meaning intent or conscious disregard of an obvious risk of fire. The defendant only forgot to turn off the stove, which is at most ordinary negligence, and intoxication doesn't supply malice. I don't agree with the team note: arson is itself the felony, so a conviction doesn't depend on a separate felony, and that is why C is wrong.

CONFIDENCE: 85
